title: The Old House Clock

full_text:
For two hundred years, the grandfather clock had ticked against the oak-paneled wall: "Tick, tack! Tick, tack!" It had seen babies christened, young lovers married, and old men carried to the grave.

The young pendulum swung with mechanical perfection, never rushing, never lagging.

"Why do you never stop to rest?" asked the restless parlor fire.

"Because every heartbeat of time is a sacred gift to mortals," ticked the clock. "Once an hour has flown, all the gold of kings cannot buy it back. Use your moments for love and truth while the pendulum swings!"
moral: Time ticks steadily for both prince and pauper; live each hour with purpose and kindness.
